title: Anyone able to make a good looking Unity project using ai?
author: Nicstar543
selftext: I’ve got an MCP hooked up to codex and some forest assets I purchased, just trying to work on graphics for now after I had done some other stuff but man this shit is ugly, it seems like the ai is unable to make any sort of lighting/bloom/visual post processing effects. Anyone else run into this? About to just give up because it’s been nearly a week of usage on the 100 dollar plan and it just seems like it’s going in circles. Am I doing something wrong or not understanding correctly? I’m a noob at unity.

comments.author: Cute-Sandwich-7207
comments.body: Which AI do you use? Do you use the web version, the CLI, or, for example, Codex, Cloudcode, or Cowork? What’s your approach? In any case, it’s essential to have a harness—rules that your AI must follow during certain processes. That’s the most important thing of all.

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body: Go look up tutorials on lighting/bloom/visual post processing effects or read the docs on unity. Having a base understanding what it does so you can give the proper termonligy to AI will push it farther than you think it would.  Also when things seem likes it loops start a new chat to help it get out of the loop. YOu have to remember ai isn't 'smart' it just knows how to pull up content it has learned. So matching key terms that are correct will ai it more.

comments.author: 0bscuris
comments.body:
I think the issue with ai is that two groups are overhyping it. The ai companies because they want everyone to use it and the ai haters for their own reasons, typically because it’s competing with them but also social credit. 

In my view having messed with it a good bit, ai is a first draft machine, not a final product machine. Think of ai as ur dumbest coworker. It can produce, but you need to be specific in what you want and really check the output. 

It performs better when u know the field it is trying to generate cuz u can be more specific in the prompt snd you can tell it, no not like that. And you can trouble shoot problems and you can just jump in and fix it if you need too.

replies.author: Nicstar543
replies.body: Yeah it seems to be really good at Java script games and atrocious at anything that uses an engine

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body:
If i was starting all over in game development today, with ai and i do this now when it’s doing some code i don’t understand. 

I tell it, explain to me line by line the code ur doing. 

Or tell it to put notes next to every line of code saying what that line does. 

It’s not something you’d want to leave in a final product but for playtesting and prototyping it is fine.

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body: There's also a surprising amount of times that you'll do this and it'll catch itself going "wait, this doesn't make sense, why did I do this?" and refactor into a much more elegant solution.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body:
I use cursor with Godot, usually a more lightweight model for most things and right now opus if I think something is more complicated. And I will also say that I spent a bit of time learning Godot but not much on gdscript. I’m making a platformer that probably will be about as complicated as super Mario world. comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body:
Look up the official name of the effect you want, remember the AI is going to give you vastly different results if you ask for "Bloom" vs "Real-Time Glow with Gaussian blur". Because it will pull data from differently skilled people.

Also all the popular VFX are extremely well explored and easy to lookup online. you often get the shader with it: [https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems/part-iv-image-processing/chapter-21-real-time-glow](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems/part-iv-image-processing/chapter-21-real-time-glow)

comments.author: Emotional_Resort_207
comments.body:
lmao. its crazy to me how ppl expect AI to do everything. it's actually incredible how far it's come and how much an AI with Unity MCP can do but dude do your own lighting and post processing that's the fun part, consult AI while u do it yourself if u wish, take screenshot of what you have, find a reference online or photoshop what you want, ask AI how to go from A to B screenshot, or give up and try again next year if u expect it to handle that much for you.  
  
Turn on post processing on ur camera, put a global post processing volume, add light sources, make it moody, turn on bloom, toy with it, add color grading and whatnot and toy with the mood, perhaps some LUTs to try some different moods. AI is good for planning, game systems, bug fixing, editor scripts, refactoring, code completion, boilerplate code, documentation. It's not that great at scene agnostic things yet though it can try. Idk why you'd want AI to do the creative and artistic fun parts of your project though.

replies.body: I don’t expect it to do everything I’m making all the pixel art characters and enemies and items and animations, I just don’t know jack about setting up 3d scenes and graphical effects and I own a construction company so don’t have a ton of time to learn. I just wanted to know if it was capable of doing it in the first plce

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
Dont try to get the AI to "just do it."  Unity is very GUI based and trying to get an AI to edit properties of .asset files is a recipe for nightmarish corruption and nonsense.

Instead, split your work between *design work* and *code work*.  Hand the code to the AI - give it a brief and tell it to go to work writing C# scripts.  Hash out the design in plain language in a chat context, and tell the AI to walk you through creating that effect in the Unity IDE - where to click, what the parameters do, what to set them to, etc.  

You'll have much better results.

replies.author: Nicstar543
replies.body: That’s actually a really good idea thanks!

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body: No problem.  You also get the bonus of learning through doing - spend enough time wiring up components in unity and you'll start getting the hang of it yourself instead of just following the AI instructions.  You'll also start catching it on its bullshit (like making multiple serialized vars for the same object instead of just referencing it multiple times)

comments.author: Sufficient_Crew_5321
comments.body: AI can definitely speed up parts of development, but making a game look good usually comes down to art direction rather than the tools being used. I've seen projects with impressive AI-generated assets still feel unpolished because the styles, colors, lighting, and UI didn't work well together. A consistent visual style, proper lighting, and a clean interface often have a bigger impact than highly detailed assets. AI is useful for prototyping and asset generation, but developers still need to make creative decisions to achieve a professional look.
